Example: {"type":"counter","counter":"CTU","instance":"ctuParts","input":{"name":"xPartEdge"},"pv":{"name":"wTarget"},"q":{"name":"xBatchDone"}}. (5) fb - the generic FB instance, for EVERY library or project-internal FunctionBlock that is not a plain timer/counter. REQUIRED instruction, instance (string or {name}), input{name} (BOOL contact wired to the FB's FIRST input pin: CTU=CU, R_TRIG=CLK, TON=IN - a data-only FB whose first pin is not BOOL must be wrapped in an ST FUNCTION_BLOCK with a BOOL first pin), outputs{EXACTLY ONE port: target} (a second output is rejected plcopen_project_fb_single_output; that one output is emitted as a coil). OPTIONAL inputs{PORT:expr} (data pins, port names matched case-insensitively, CONSTANT LITERALS ALLOWED here - unlike generic box pins). Example: {"type":"fb","instruction":"R_TRIG","instance":"rtStart","input":{"name":"xStart"},"outputs":{"Q":"xStartEdge"}}. WHEN box/fb IS MANDATORY, NOT OPTIONAL: any time- or count-dependent behaviour (ON/OFF delay, pulse, PWM duty, batch count, totalizer), edge detection and every 'act once per press' step, comparisons (GT/GE/LT/LE/EQ/NE), arithmetic (ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV/MOD), selection (SEL/MUX/LIMIT/MIN/MAX), conversions, string functions, and EVERY user-FB or library-FB instance. NEVER emulate a timer or a counter with self-holding contacts or by counting scans: contact/coil networks have no time base and no count state, the phase drifts with the task period, and the defect is INVISIBLE at compile time (E2E V2 R053: a PWM period emulated with a self-holding contact kept running through the stop cycle - measured 347 ms against a nominal 2000 ms high time; only codesys_sim_assert exposed it; the fix was an explicit command contact in series with the seal-in leg). contact_coil is ONLY for genuinely Boolean relay logic: seal-in, interlock, permissive chain, lamp/valve drive. POU NAME: pass `name`, the required field in this tool schema. The bridge also accepts block_name/pouName internally for compatibility; use name in public calls. The name must be a non-reserved IEC identifier and must NOT equal an instruction name. READBACK COUNT SEMANTICS (E2E V2 R050): readbackCounts.coil/contact count every output line and every pin contact â€” a fb network's Q output line counts as a coil and its CLK/IN pin contact counts as a contact, so 2 contact_coil networks + 1 fb network can report coil=3 / contact=7. Compare the network SHAPE, not the raw counts. The bridge emits deterministic PLCopen TC6 XML, imports it through the Ladder plugin's own converter, then checks that native-export readback contains graphical nodes (ladderBodyVerified + readbackCounts). These fields prove node presence only, not correct wiring or requested control behaviour; use selected block readback and appropriate logic tests for those claims â€” a clean compile alone is NOT proof of a real LAD body. IMPORT LOCATION (E2E V1 R036 false-green trap): the POU lands in the resolved device Application node (result carries parent + importedPath) â€” never the project root, where build.compile passes 0/0/0 while the POU does not participate; pass parent only to place it elsewhere. ACCEPTANCE: ladderBodyVerified + readbackCounts AND a final whole-project compile with the POU in the task call list (codesys_task_pou_set) â€” an unreferenced POU compiles clean but never runs. TYPE CONTRACT (E2E V1 R036): CODESYS standard-library CTU/CTD/CTUD are WORD-typed â€” bind pv/cv to WORD variables (or literal values 0..65535), NOT DINT/INT. NOT GENERATABLE (verified absent on the vanilla line): SET/RESET COILS and negated coils, MOVE box, constant literals on generic box inputs, initial values on variables[] â€” use SR/RS FB networks for latches, R_TRIG/F_TRIG FB networks for edges, and SEL chains for conditional assignment. FB NETWORKS (type "fb"): a generic FunctionBlock instance â€” {instruction, instance, input:{name} (BOOL contact wired to the FIRST input pin â€” for CTU that pin is CU, i.e. the COUNT-ENABLE contact, not a power rail; for R_TRIG it is CLK; for TON it is IN), inputs:{PORT: expr} (data pins, CONSTANT LITERALS ALLOWED â€” unlike generic box pins), outputs:{FIRST_OUTPUT_PORT: target}}; ONLY the first output pin can be wired (the Ladder plugin editor rejects a second output, 2026-09-08 verified). instruction may be a library FB OR a PROJECT-INTERNAL user FB (E2E V2 R031 verified: a user FB created on the ST channel is called from LAD with this shape, 0/0) â€” this generator only creates PROGRAM POUs, so an FB-shaped deliverable means: ST channel creates the FB body, LAD fb networks instance and call it. The instance is auto-declared in the POU's local vars â€” do NOT also declare the same name in a GVL (silent duplicate). The timer/counter kinds are the SAME shape with friendlier fields. MACHINE-VERIFIED FBs (probe 2026-09-09: import + native-export readback + task call + whole-PLC 0/0): TON/TOF/TP/CTU/CTD/CTUD plus SR (SET1 bus / RESET data -> Q1), RS (SET bus / RESET1 data -> Q1), R_TRIG (CLK -> Q), F_TRIG (CLK -> Q). NOT in the local catalog (rejected before import with instruction_signature_unresolved): BLINK (the Util library is not referenced by the Standard.project template) and TONR (no signature) â€” do not plan on either. SCAN SEMANTICS (E2E V2 R024, verified 33-network shift at 0/0): coils evaluate in network order and a coil reads the value written EARLIER THIS SCAN â€” a shift register MUST compute the next state into temp bits first, then copy temp->state in a LATER network (ascending copy double-sets the wrap bit; descending copy dead-locks at all-zero). A pure-OR network (no series contacts) is driven from an always-ON GVL bool (`xAlwaysOn : BOOL := TRUE;`) â€” the machine-verified form; an empty contacts[] with branches is ALSO the accepted pure-OR form (validator + emitter contract), so pick either; timer pt.constant_value accepts T#500MS literals verbatim and readback echoes them (T#8h also verified, E2E V2 R029). DECLARATION CONTRACT (E2E V2 R029): the generator auto-declares FB INSTANCES only â€” contact/coil/q/pt/pv TARGET variables must be declared by YOU (GVL or variables[]); a missing one compiles to æ²¡æœ‰å®ä¹‰æ ‡è¯†ç¬¦ at the whole-project build while this tool's own diagnostics stay 0. The result lists pouLocalUndeclaredReferences (names not declared in THIS POU's own interface/variables) plus resolvedInGlobalScope (of those, found in a project GVL) and missingEverywhere (in neither) â€” declare the missingEverywhere names before the first build. To add variables to an existing GVL use codesys_pou_add_variable (verified); full declaration rewrites still need delete+recreate. Box networks need NO series contacts â€” enable defaults to TRUE (omit it or pass enable:{name} for gating); a single-output function box may feed its output back into its own input (ADD and SEL both verified: accumulators and hold-latches). ALGORITHMIC WORK (arrays, indexing, loops) is NOT expressible in these network shapes â€” put it in an ST-channel POU (codesys_pou_upsert / codesys_source_import) and keep LAD as the operation/IO layer (E2E V2 R031/R033 verified architecture). A FUNCTION-shaped deliverable maps to a PROGRAM POU whose interface lives in a GVL (VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT semantics = GVL members, E2E V2 R035 verified: 0/0). VERIFIED SHAPES (E2E V2 R027, 41-network PID at 0/0): a box whose output feeds back into its OWN input of the same name is a legal accumulator (`ADD IN1:=rIAcc -> rIAcc` does rIAcc += term â€” verified by native readback); without a MOVE box, copy a variable with `ADD(IN1:=src, IN2:=rZero)`; analog direct addresses AT %IW0/%QW0 compile 0/0 on the Control Win V3 soft PLC. TABLE INTERPOLATION (E2E V2 R038, 6-segment cam table at 0/0): expand a lookup as an ASCENDING chain of `GE(phase>=P_k)` gated `SEL` segments â€” later segments win (descending order fails: the k=0 leg is always-true and overwrites everything); task call order (task_pou_set pous array order) IS the same-scan data-visibility order, so a MAIN->CAM->OUT chain passes data forward through GVL members in one scan. TIME CONTRACT (E2E V2 R025, 4 compile errors evidence): box DIV/MUL/ADD evaluate DINT/REAL ONLY â€” TIME never participates in arithmetic, there is NO DINT_TO_TIME, and pt accepts only TIME literals or TIME variable names, so LAD ITSELF cannot COMPUTE a period. A variable-PT timer IS usable when the TIME value is computed elsewhere (E2E V2 R036 verified: `pt:{name: tPulsePeriod}` with tPulsePeriod computed in an ST-channel POU, 0/0) â€” for LAD-only variable duty/frequency use the verified pattern instead: a TP timebase (pt = TIME literal) + two CTU counters (PV WORD-typed from the GVL) with the effective timebase = PT + task period compensated by a GVL constant (18 networks, 0/0). The schema's et/cv fields EXIST but are NOT wired (Q only) â€” never plan on reading ET/CV. VERIFIED REGISTRY (real-machine, 142 library instructions + 23 IEC built-in operators, every batch import + readback + precompile 0/0/0, 2026-09-08): 6 FunctionBlocks CTU/CTD/CTUD/TOF/TON/TP; 24 typed comparisons (INT64__EQ/NE/GT/GE/LT/LE, REAL32__*, REAL64__*, UINT64__*...); 28 typed arithmetic (INT32/INT64/REAL32/REAL64/UINT64 __ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV/MOD/ABS; NOTE E2E V2 R034: INT32__ADD answers not_found on live queries on this machine â€” use the built-in ADD operator instead, verified 0/0); 23 typed conversions (X__TO__Y casts + NEW__REAL32__TO__STRING/WSTRING); 9 STANDARD string functions CONCAT/DELETE/FIND/INSERT/LEFT/LEN/MID/REPLACE/RIGHT; 24 typed math (REAL32/REAL64 __SIN/COS/TAN/ASIN/ACOS/ATAN/EXP/EXPT/LN/LOG/SQRT/TRUNC); 4 typed logic (UINT64__AND/OR/XOR/NOT); 14 typed LIMIT/MAX/MIN; 10 typed shifts (UINT32/UINT64/INT32/INT64 __ROL/ROR/SHL/SHR). EXCLUDED (internal/context, each pinned by a real diagnostic): ADDR/ID/MAKE_EVENTID/CODEM*/EVENT*/GETSUPPLIERVERSION/SLOT_ID/SUBSLOT_ID/RESMANINCHARGE/LEN_INTERNAL/MYSTRING_TO_UDINT/MYUDINT_TO_STRING/ANY*__TO__*/multi-output functions. Network kinds: (1) contact_coil: series contacts[] (each {name, negated?} â€” negated=true is the NC contact) + optional branches[] (>=2 parallel OR legs, each {contacts:[...]}) + one coil {target}; semantics: coil = (OR of branch legs) AND (AND of series contacts); branch+NC verified as ONE network on the real machine. (2) box: one Function instruction with port-keyed inputs/outputs maps â€” instruction may be an IEC built-in operator (NOT in the library catalog): compare GT/LT/GE/LE/EQ/NE ports IN1,IN2 -> <the INSTRUCTION NAME>; arithmetic ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV ports IN1,IN2 -> <the INSTRUCTION NAME>; selection SEL (G:BOOL,IN0,IN1), MUX (K,IN0,IN1), LIMIT (MN,IN,MX), MAX/MIN (IN1,IN2); math ABS/SQRT/TRUNC (IN -> <the INSTRUCTION NAME>); conversions INT_TO_REAL/REAL_TO_INT/BOOL_TO_INT/INT_TO_BOOL/WORD_TO_INT/INT_TO_WORD (IN -> <the INSTRUCTION NAME>). The output pin of a box is the instruction name itself, NOT the word 'result' (E2E R027: MUL with outputs.result was rejected, knownPins=[MUL]); read codesys_lad_instruction_signatures when unsure; an instruction with no live catalog or built-in entry is rejected with instruction_signature_unresolved (E2E R032: REAL_TO_DWORD), so pick a name from the registry/list above or query the signatures first â€” or a library instruction from the VERIFIED REGISTRY above whose pins the bridge resolves live. The box is emitted as ONE series rung (contact(enable)->EN); ONLY ONE data output per box (the plugin editor rejects more with 'too many outputs'); string/wstring variables are legal (the emitter writes TC6-legal lowercase string elements). (3) timer: TON/TOF/TP â€” instance + input{name} (BOOL power contact) + pt{constant_value:T#..s|name} + q{name}; v1 emits Q only. - LAD: codesys_lad_generate_project_pou is THE generator — ONE call = ONE PROGRAM POU with the complete networks[] array (each element = one network, max 60). NETWORK TYPES — EXACT MEASURED SURFACE (2026-09-10): contact_coil | box | timer | counter | fb; timer/counter are sugar over fb. Timers, counters, edge detection, comparisons (GT/GE/LT/LE/EQ/NE), arithmetic (ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV/MOD), selection (SEL/MUX/LIMIT/MIN/MAX), conversions, string functions and EVERY user-FB/library-FB instance MUST be a box/fb/timer/counter network — contact_coil is ONLY for genuinely Boolean relay logic (seal-in, interlock, permissive chain, lamp/valve drive). NEVER emulate a time- or count-dependent behaviour with self-holding contacts: a contact/coil network has no time base and no count state, the phase drifts with the task period, and the defect stays invisible until a runtime sim_assert (E2E V2 R053: PWM emulated with a self-holding contact ran on through the stop cycle — measured 347 ms against a nominal 2000 ms). It imports the POU into the device Application node automatically (parent optional; result carries parent/importedPath). INSTRUCTION DISCOVERY: Use the current tool card or a still-valid prior lookup when it already supplies the exact instruction, kind and pins with the required types; do not rediscover them before generating. Search only when the instruction name or kind is unknown (codesys_lad_instruction_search with a targeted query); when the exact name is known, query codesys_lad_instruction_signatures directly only when its required pin/type contract is missing or ambiguous, batching the needed names[] in one call. A search result's pin names alone do not establish missing types or library availability. A LAD fb network accepts library FBs and project-internal user FBs. If current diagnostics identify a missing library reference, resolve that specific reference before querying again. IEC built-in operators (ADD/GT/SEL/conversions) use the tool card's supported shapes and do not require a library catalog search.- LAD acceptance (all three gates): (1) the POU must live under the Application node — a root-level import is OUTSIDE the compiled application and yields a false-green 0/0/0 (E2E V1 R036; the generator now prevents it, but verify parent/importedPath when you imported manually); (2) ladderBodyVerified=true with readbackCounts>0 from the native-export readback; (3) the POU is in the task call list (codesys_task_pou_set) AND the whole-project build has acceptanceVerdict=pass, with warnings assessed. Import success or a clean compile ALONE is not proof of a LAD body: an empty shell or an unreferenced POU both compile 0/0/0.- LAD shapes (real-machine verified): series contacts plus one-level parallel branches are ONE connected network (the importer splits networks by connectivity); a box sits on the power path with series EN wiring and EXACTLY ONE data output (more outputs are rejected); timers/counters emit Q only in v1 (ET/CV unwired), so multi-segment timing and flashing use MULTIPLE TON instances — budget the extra networks; TC6 string/wstring elements must be lowercase; never name a variable after an instruction name.- Comments carrier (E2E V2 R023 LAD / R042 ST): on the LAD channel, networks and POU variables have NO comment fields — Chinese comments live in the GVL declaration text (compiled 0/0, verified); POU-local variables stay uncommented by construction. On the ST channel the OPPOSITE holds: Chinese comments go directly into the POU declaration/implementation text (`(* 中文 *)` read back exactMatch, whole-project 0/0 verified, E2E V2 R042) — never strip ST comments because of the LAD rule. GVL declarations also carry variable INITIAL VALUES (POU variables[] cannot), e.g. an always-ON rail `xRun : BOOL := TRUE;`, AND AT direct addresses — %IX/%QX/%IW/%QW/%ID/%QD (scalar AND array forms, e.g. `aiRaw AT %IW0 : ARRAY[1..10] OF INT;` and the bit-array form `axLamp AT %QX0.0 : ARRAY[0..7] OF BOOL;` which fills %QB0 — both compile 0/0, E2E V2 R021/R027/R028/R032/R033/R044). Array whole-assignment works across blocks with no FOR loop: `GVL_IO.axLamp := fbRun.axLamp;` (FB VAR_OUTPUT array -> GVL array) compiled 0/0 (E2E V2 R044). AT SYNTAX ORDER (E2E V2 R034): `name AT %addr : TYPE;` — name FIRST, AT second, type LAST; the reverse order (`name : TYPE AT %addr;`) fails with 7 errors `应该采用';, :=, REF=, ( 或 [' 取代'AT'`.- Compile order (E2E V2 R024/R033): the Standard.project template device may be a PLACEHOLDER (3.1.3.0) or already upgraded (earlier rounds migrated the on-disk template) — build BEFORE device.update fails with 16 errors (`系统没有安装设备。不能生成代码`) in the placeholder case, and the SP19->SP22 storage-format migration runs on first open either way. Order: create -> device.update (once, then save) -> author -> compile.- SIMULATION PHASE (E2E V2 R048, re-verified natively in R052, machine-verified): this line CAN verify program behaviour at runtime. codesys_sim_status is the phase gate (call it when a simulation step is actually next); codesys_sim_set switches the project's simulation mode; codesys_sim_online reports or releases the live session; codesys_sim_read / codesys_sim_write are batch runtime I/O; codesys_sim_assert runs ONE ordered scenario (steps[] with expect / expectWithinMs / expectNotBeforeMs / holdMs) and returns a verdict plus the value really read; codesys_sim_force_clear clears forced values. The session lives INSIDE the resident bridge on the project it has open (no second IDE process, no project copy) and logs in automatically on first use, so sim I/O may start a stopped app. For first-scan inputs use explicit codesys_online_reset -> codesys_online_write (keeps STOP) -> codesys_online_start; a later preset or stop/start does not recreate a first scan. codesys_sim_online action=stop ends the simulation session. Runtime evidence is a FOURTH acceptance gate: compile 0/0 + structure readback + the POU in the task call list + a passing scenario. Timing: there is no breakpoint/step support, so a stimulus is write -> wait >=N task cycles -> read; a written input is NOT a persistent force, so keep the stimulus HELD while it must span scans, and prove a delay with expectNotBeforeMs + expectWithinMs. Force hygiene: writing an expression that is FORCED raises StandardError, so clear forces first. Author + save the program first, then assert. BOUNDARY: simulation evaluates program LOGIC only — no I/O wiring, fieldbus or hardware is evaluated, and 'simulation pass' is never 'wiring correct'.- IO ADDRESS ALIASING (E2E V2 R047, caught by a runtime scenario): a word address occupies a WHOLE BYTE RANGE — %IW0 covers %IB0+%IB1, %QW0 covers %QB0+%QB1 — so digital bits %IX0.0..%IX0.7 / %QX0.0..%QX0.7 are the SAME memory. A scenario wrote an analog value into %IW0 and silently cleared the E-stop bit in %IX0.x, so the program refused to run; keep analog words and digital bits on DISJOINT bytes (e.g. analog on bytes 0/1, digital from byte 2) and assert the interlock input inside the same scenario.- Runtime evidence is per SESSION (E2E V2 R047/R052): the session belongs to ONE program version — re-authoring and saving the project makes the next sim call log in again, which restarts the simulated program and shows INITIAL values. Collect every assertion of one proof in ONE codesys_sim_assert scenario; a separate read after re-authoring is not evidence about the same run.- Runtime verification: stop/start, login and preset stop_write_start do not establish initial values; read actual baselines. For reinitialization use ToolSearch select=[codesys_online_reset], simulation on=true first. Warm retains RETAIN/PERSISTENT and initializes ordinary variables; Cold also clears RETAIN; Original removes the application. Read the returned post-reset state with codesys_sim_status before continuing (sim_read/sim_assert can start execution). Verify values, not the reset label; simulator reset does not prove physical power-loss persistence. codesys_sim_online action=stop disables simulation; select codesys_sim_set on=true before further simulation. Keep stimulus and edge checks in the same step, use observed sample timing, and read evidence.path for an archived complete report.- Same-step anchoring (E2E V2 R053, measured): the write that creates a stimulus and the edge it is judged by must live in the SAME step — the observed sample cadence is a few hundred ms, so a separate write step leaves the phase baseline to the previous step. Every step row reports elapsedMs (measured boundary time from its write to the condition holding) and sampleCadenceMs (observed sampling interval); size the measured interval far above the cadence.- Deleting objects after simulation (E2E V2 R053, vendor error 无法移除对象…因为该对象已经用于当前登录的设备): while the sim/online session is logged in the device holds the Application and object.delete is refused. codesys_object_delete now returns object_delete_blocked_by_online_session with data.requiredAction {tool:codesys_sim_online, action:stop} and keeps the vendor text in data.rawVendorMessage (autoLogout=true releases the session in the same call), so run codesys_sim_online action=stop BEFORE the cleanup order task entry -> POU -> GVL.- Runtime verification (E2E V2 R024/R048): timing and sequence claims have a runtime channel (the SIMULATION PHASE tools above). PROGRAM POUs cannot be instantiated in VAR blocks — call them directly by name (`MyProgram();`) and declare instances only for FUNCTION_BLOCKs. ST supports TIME arithmetic, comparison AND conversion (`xOk := (T_RED = T_GREEN + T_YELLOW);` and `rPeriod := DINT_TO_REAL(TIME_TO_DINT(tTaskPeriod));` both compiled 0/0, E2E V2 R043/R045) — the LAD 'TIME never participates in arithmetic' contract is a LAD box-pin limitation, NOT an ST one; do not carry it across channels. ST declaration TEXT may also carry initial values (`rPhaseMs : REAL := 0.0;` 0/0, E2E V2 R045) — the 'no initial values' rule applies only to the LAD generator's variables[] JSON. TYPE CONVERSION CONTRACT (E2E V2 R053, vendor error text): a conversion function only accepts its own source type — INT_TO_REAL takes an INT, so feeding a DINT expression fails to compile with 不能将类型 'DINT' 转换为类型'INT' (行43,列1 (Impl)); use the conversion that names the argument's declared type (DINT_TO_REAL for a DINT) instead of relying on implicit widening, and check the declared type before picking the X_TO_Y name.- ST acceptance (all three gates, E2E V2 R042): a written POU compiles 0/0 even when NO task calls it — verify (1) codesys_pou_upsert / codesys_gvl_create readback exactMatch, (2) whole-project build.compile acceptanceVerdict=pass (warnings assessed separately), (3) the POU is in the intended task call list: a successful codesys_task_pou_set receipt with exactReadback=true and after matching the requested list already verifies this gate; use codesys_task_list only when that evidence is missing, mismatched or stale after a project/task change. Same false-green family as the LAD root-POU trap (V1 R036). This structure</MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="12"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US"> is configured to hold all the data required by the card itself, any module accessing an analog output</MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="13"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US"> and any supervisory system that is to display the type and configuration of the output channel.</MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="14"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US"> </MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="15"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US">All the channel data is stored as constants and is used by all modules that have an interface </MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="16"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US">to an analog output card.</MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="17"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US"> </MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="18"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US">The purpose of the user data type and associated data block is to provide a consistent and </MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="19"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US">tested set of range, parameter and descriptive data that can be used directly by modules that </MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="20"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US">interface with analog output cards.</MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="21"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US"> </MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="22"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US">The ranges correspond to the numerical values required by the card for a given type of analog card </MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="23"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US">signal. For example, a 4-20 mA card requires a numerical value of 0 to generate an output of </MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="24"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US">4 mA ranging up to a value of 27648 at 20 mA. The data specified in the UT00802 variable would </MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="25"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US">have a lower limit of 0 and an upper limit of 27648.</MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="26"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US"> </MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="27"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US">In addition, each dataset contains the parametric data that defines the particular channel type and </MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="28"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US">can be used to set a particular analog output channel to a particular type and range during</MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="29"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US">runtime. Each dataset also contains a textual description of the channel type, </MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="30"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US">e.g. Current (4 mA to 20 mA)</MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement Path="31"><Comment><MultiLanguageText Lang="en-US">for display and information purposes.</MultiLanguageText></Comment></Subelement><Subelement ===== RVA 045A34D9 len=11172 =====
Route rules for Inovance InoProShop (CODESYS-based; LAD and ST):InoProShop high-throughput execution path (apply the phases the request actually needs):- The staging workspace is the local binder, not the live IDE project. Reuse fresh operation/environment facts to decide reuse versus a new project; bootstrap already checks the live project and reports closedPrevious. Recheck when facts may be stale or another actor changed the IDE, and preserve unrelated projects.- Chain deterministic dependent bridge mutations into ONE inoproshop_batch call (steps=[{tool,input}], stops at the first failing step; earlier steps stay executed). The COMPOSITE tools inoproshop_project_bootstrap / inoproshop_project_finalize / inoproshop_program_deploy / inoproshop_object_regenerate are NOT batchable steps — call them directly, one per call. Generator/registry/search/outline tools (codesys_lad_generate_*, codesys_lad_*_instructions, codesys_read_*) are NOT batchable either — call them directly.- Program: establish interfaces/ownership, prove a representative slice, then expand dependencies (GVL/DUT -> called POU -> caller). Each LAD generation needs one complete POU networks array; same-name replacement uses the documented delete/regenerate path after preserving existing source. Bind caller data explicitly.- Use the selected generator contract when it supplies the required pins/types/structure. For missing details, consult the current signatures/catalog or applicable evidence once. Follow matchKind/suggestion on rejection; do not guess alternative names or repeat unchanged rejected plans.- Direct GVL AT %IX/%QX scalar IO compiled on the tested AM600-CPU1608TP/TN; this does not validate wiring or other device layouts. Use the actual target address widths and avoid overlaps. Generators may add required references; inspect their receipt. An instruction missing from a project does not prove its library is unavailable: check installed libraries AND project references.- Avoid unchanged repeated saves/compiles and one-call-per-object deletes when a suitable batch exists. Save meaningful recovery checkpoints before risky changes and at delivery; a long session may need several. Compile after edits or changed target/environment, and distinguish syntax checking from code generation/download validation. Reuse tool facts rather than rediscovering bridge paths through PowerShell.- Compile/repair: read data.acceptanceVerdict with the current diagnostics. pass requires explicit completed build/precompile evidence and no errors; ordinary warnings alone do not make fail. fail means a reported failure; inconclusive means proof is incomplete. Preserve errorCode, gateFailures and diagnosticGaps; do not turn a typed failure into pass from a zero count. For lad_preexisting_diagnostics, refresh once with inoproshop_build_compile and retry only when its receipt supports that remedy. Repair the affected POU and verify the final changed artifact; unchanged repeated compiles add no proof.- GENERATOR PATH (LAD blocks, small, no research): codesys_lad_generate_native IS the LAD generator — ONE call = ONE POU with the complete networks array; the exact port tables (SR: SET1/RESET->Q1; BLINK: ENABLE/TIMELOW/TIMEHIGH->OUT; TON/TOF/TP/CTU/CTD/CTUD/R_TRIG/F_TRIG) are INLINE in that tool's own description, and BLINK needs no library. Happy path: inoproshop_project_bootstrap -> inoproshop_gvl_create (declare AT %IX/%QX IO directly in the GVL) -> ONE codesys_lad_generate_native -> inoproshop_project_finalize. For a complete multi-object program (GVL declaration + ST implementation + LAD networks + task binding in one shot) use the 3-call shortcut instead: inoproshop_project_bootstrap -> inoproshop_program_deploy -> inoproshop_project_finalize. Use the inline contract directly when sufficient. If required pins, types or plan structure remain unknown, make a targeted spec or private-case lookup before generating; do not repeat catalog/research calls for facts already available.- NAMESPACE PREWARM (E2E V2 R090, measured on AM600-CPU1608TP/TN, fixed): the FIRST codesys_lad_generate_native on a freshly created project used to fail at validate_plan with SIGNATURE_SELECTOR_NOT_FOUND expected=STANDARD candidates=[] because the STANDARD namespace is only registered after the project has been compiled once. The generator now runs that single offline build itself and retries the SAME plan exactly once — read data.namespacePrewarm ({performed,build,retried,recoveredOnRetry,originalFailure}) — so do NOT insert a manual inoproshop_build_compile before generating: generate first, then take inoproshop_project_finalize's whole-project compile as the acceptance verdict. The trigger requires EVERY failure to be SIGNATURE_SELECTOR_NOT_FOUND with an EMPTY candidates[]; this does not prove that the requested instruction exists. Read data.namespacePrewarm: do not repeat a manual compile plus unchanged generation after performed=true and retried=true. If it still fails, use the final diagnostics and originalFailure to check the requested instruction/namespace against the current live catalog. If performed=false or buildError is present, fix the reported build/environment prerequisite before retrying; an incomplete prewarm does not prove the instruction is absent.- Cleanup while a session is logged in (E2E V2 R053): the vendor refuses object.delete with 无法移除对象…因为该对象已经用于当前登录的设备. codesys_object_delete now answers object_delete_blocked_by_online_session with data.requiredAction {tool:codesys_sim_online, action:stop}, data.onlineSession and the vendor text verbatim in data.rawVendorMessage (pass autoLogout=true to release the session in the same call). Run codesys_sim_online action=stop BEFORE deleting, in the order task entry -> POU -> GVL.- Contact/rung plans (pure contacts+coils+timers with power flow) use codesys_lad_generate_contact_block with its own plan schema. Everything else goes to codesys_lad_generate_native. All other codesys_lad_* cards (instruction_spec / list_instructions / search_instructions / generate_native_template / recipes / template_evidence / read_outline) are diagnostic-only — never call them for a small fresh task.- The always-on InoProShop surface already covers the complete program-generation/authoring path (LAD generators, GVL/POU/ST/task/project/build/symbol/IO tools). The remaining bridge families are ON-DEMAND GROUPS — activate one with inoproshop_open_tool_group (pass several group_ids in ONE call) only when the task actually needs that family:- This route drives InoProShop V1.10.0.3 (CODESYS-based) through the resident file-IPC bridge (route_cli.py). AM300/AM400/AM500/AM600/AM800 CPUs are the inoproshop family.- Expose only instruction IDs returned by the verified generator registry and the 896-entry native template/operator set. A runtime lookup or vendor documentation entry alone is reference data, not a generator. If an ID is absent, reject generation with the structured remediation from codesys_lad_instruction_spec; never synthesize a guessed box.- All project writes require disposable=true (JSON boolean) plus the exact confirm token; the bridge refuses writes outside the disposable experiment root.- If bridge.status says bridge_not_ready or ide_not_running, there is NO startup tool to call: any project operation (inoproshop_project_status, inoproshop_project_bootstrap, ...) starts the resident bridge on demand through route_cli, and that on-demand start LAUNCHES the InoProShop IDE itself when it is not already running (the IDE window appears; the first call can take tens of seconds — wait for its response instead of re-issuing the call). Only the bridge probes answer without starting anything (inoproshop_bridge_status says so on its own card, codesys_bridge_capabilities likewise); every project/object/build/online/simulation tool needs the IDE. Just proceed with the operation you need; record readiness evidence from its response. If the start fails, the response names the failure (environment-facts / heartbeat) — report that, never a guessed cause.- Report material generation failures and their evidence. Classify precompile diagnostics by cause: invalid plan/arguments, pre-existing project diagnostics, missing libraries/types, or generator/import implementation errors. A precompile error alone does not prove a generator defect. A clean compile alone does not prove requested behaviour.- The disposable experiment root is machine-canonical: <LOCALAPPDATA>\PLC Code\codesys-bridge\vendor-experiments (the CODESYS_ROUTE_DISPOSABLE_ROOT override may pin a different one). Create new projects under it; a path outside it fails with unsafe_project_path.- For plc_experience_read/plc_experience_update on this route, prefer OMITTING route_key so the engine derives it from the bound project. If you must hand-write it, the derived key is vendor/inovance/family/inoproshop/model/<defaultModel-ascii-lowercased-with-/-to-_>/language/xml/integration/inoproshop_bridge/openness/not_tia — do NOT write language/lad or openness/v1.10 (those segments are wrong for this route and would land in a store the runtime never reads).- Some tested templates had unresolved #InoParamsConfigLib or #SoftMotion_AddRamps placeholders. Diagnose current library references/resolution separately from POU errors; this is an installation/template finding, not a permanent platform limit. For lad_preexisting_diagnostics refresh build diagnostics once before retrying unchanged.- Installation inventory on THIS line: codesys_system_list_installations (this line's profiles / executables / repository paths). The vanilla-CODESYS Installer inventory (codesys_installer_list_installations via APInstaller.CLI) belongs to the OTHER line — never read a vanilla machine's state through it and vice versa.- GENERATOR PATH (ST task, no research): a pure-ST program does not go through the LAD generators and needs no LAD recipe/registry/instruction lookup. Author the GVL declaration and the ST body through inoproshop_program_deploy (gvlName+gvlDeclaration+stName+stDeclaration+stImplementation+task+pous) or inoproshop_pou_write, then take inoproshop_project_finalize's whole-project compile as the acceptance verdict. Happy path: inoproshop_project_bootstrap -> inoproshop_program_deploy -> inoproshop_project_finalize. MIXED ST+LAD PROJECTS ARE NOT AN EXCEPTION TO THE LAD PATH: when the same application also contains LAD blocks, choose the exchange format PER BLOCK (ST/SCL block -> the ST route above; LAD block -> the LAD GENERATOR PATH line above) — never treat 'the project is ST' as a reason to skip a LAD block, and never re-author a working block in the other language just to unify the project.PLC_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIENCE_WRITEDeliverable shape:- A whole-program request gets a complete deliverable (entry point, named blocks, instance/static state, IO/tag mapping, command/permissive/interlock/fault/output layers, validation path) rather than a throwaway demo.- When the user names a single rung/network/block, or says "just"/"only"/"a snippet"/similar, touch ONLY the named piece — do not expand it into a whole-program rebuild.engineering_lessonvendor_limitationlocal_environment

===== RVA 0344F018 len=9783 =====
mitsubishi_mc_read_wordsRead consecutive WORD devices from a Mitsubishi PLC over the MC protocol (MELSEC Communication) 3E frame - batch read (command 0401, word units). Reads count consecutive 16-bit words starting at address. Supported word devices: D, W, R, ZR, SW, SD, Z (index register), TN (timer current value), CN (counter current value), STN (retentive timer current value). A bit device (X/Y/M/L/F/V/B/S/SB/SM/DX/DY, TS/TC/CS/CC) is also accepted and read in word units: each returned value is 16 consecutive bits packed (low bit = lowest device number), and the address of each point is therefore reported as the 16-device SPAN it covers - a 2-word read of M100 comes back as M100-M115 and M116-M131, not M100 and M101. Device numbers follow the MELSEC-Q/L/iQ-R convention: W, SW, ZR, B, X, Y, DX, DY are HEXADECIMAL; D, R, SD, Z, TN, CN, STN, M, L, F, V, S are DECIMAL. Every result reports the radix it used in addressRadix, and warns in addressRadixWarning for the two families that differ on FX5/iQ-F (there X/Y follow the connection's message-format setting, and ZR is decimal where Q/L makes it hexadecimal). count is 1..960 (the MC protocol hard limit for a single word-unit batch read); read more by issuing several calls. Each returned value is an unsigned 16-bit word plus its hex form. UNVERIFIED: this MC channel has NOT been tested on a real Mitsubishi PLC and cannot be on the current bench (no Mitsubishi PLC, no GX Works installed) - the frame codec is proven offline only against the byte-level communication examples and the device-code table in the official MELSEC Communication Protocol Reference Manual SH(NA)-080008-AB, and every result says verified:false. The CPU answers MC only after the MC/SLMP connection is opened in GX Works Ethernet parameters and downloaded; connection errors explain this. transport is tcp (default) or udp. 3E frame only. tia_plcsim_assert_behaviorProve what a downloaded program actually COMPUTES on a running controller: write stimuli, wait a stated time, read the outputs back. Carry a whole verification table (10-20 groups) in ONE call as steps[] — never one set/read pair per group. The table is planned before the first write, and `stop_on_first_failure` defaults to TRUE, so every group after the first failure comes back `skipped` rather than observed — order the groups so the earliest ones establish what the later ones need, and pass `stop_on_first_failure=false` when the call is a diagnostic sweep that must return every group's reading. Put restore writes in `cleanup[]`, not as the last `steps[]` entry: cleanup runs whatever the verdict and may carry `expect`, so the restore is read back and reported instead of assumed — a restore left inside `steps` is skipped the moment an earlier step fails. Standard-area stimulus rules: V16/V17 writes use symbolic M tags (address writes there only reach bit 0); V18/V19/V20/V21 writes use the WHOLE input byte (IB0, data_type BYTE) — bit writes fail there (no input read-back); assert Q bits. Use after the CPU is in RUN — a clean compile/download/RUN proves none of the logic. The controller keeps its state between steps and between calls, so a group can start from whatever earlier work left behind: in the recorded R135 run a group passed only after `tia_plcsim_advanced_storage` (action=memory_reset) and then `tia_plcsim_advanced_set_state` (state=run) had both succeeded. If a group's result depends on state an earlier call or step left behind, read that state back in the same group before concluding (a step with no `write` is exactly that); a runtime-accepted write can also be overwritten by the program before your first reading. One call runs an ordered scenario; verdict pass/fail/error plus, per expectation, the value really read. Channel by what is running: s7-absolute drives absolute addresses (M0.0, MW10, QW0, DB1.DBD0) over S7 ISO-on-TCP (real CPU or PLCSIM Advanced in TCP/IP mode); plcsim-advanced-tag drives symbolic tags through the PLCSIM Advanced Runtime API (default Softbus); plcsim-standard-area drives the I/Q/M process image of a standard S7-PLCSIM session started with tia_plcsim_standard_start. - Match the task: interlocks, sequences/batches, timing/counting, analog/data, PID, communication, recipes/alarms/HMI or motion. A small job needs no framework. Stateless calculations need no state machine or motion-style interface.- Establish input meaning, interfaces, data/output ownership, timing and recovery. Trace physical/HMI inputs to actual consumers/tasks; declarations or Enable/Linked flags do not prove binding/readiness.- Data: check types, units, precision, ranges and validity before arithmetic/conversion. Handle applicable divide-by-zero, overflow, indexing and stale/invalid inputs. Convert before lossy integer operations when fractions matter; preserve native fault sources and types.- Stateful logic: use named states; commit next state once or equivalent to avoid scan fall-through. Timers/counters/edges keep suitable instances and receive inactive/reset inputs; skipping a call is not a reset. Check task periods, shared data and restart behavior.- Define level/edge and command priority; jog follows held input. Stop/abort must cancel pending starts in idle/recovery too; test Start+Stop together. Reset is not Start. Completion/counting needs an accepted transaction and positive success evidence; sensor clearing after fault/manual removal is not production. Reconcile pending work, readiness and counts on restart; preserve retained parameters.- Async work: follow the actual request/acceptance and success/error/abort/timeout/cancel contract. Release software ownership and re-arm inputs appropriately; abort is not completion. Require current readiness, propagate stop to active work and avoid circular waits. Clearing Busy does not prove physical completion.- Apply relevant domain checks: invalid analog/level quality must affect the relevant output permissives; PID actual operating mode/activation, real cyclic task period, direction, limits and hand/auto transfer; communication response identity/freshness/retry effects; recipe consistent application; alarm cause versus acknowledgement. Operator parameters cannot exceed fixed protection ceilings in requirements. Consult the installed contract.- Name intent; document parameters with units/ranges and reasons. One purpose per network/function, clear ownership, useful blocking/fault diagnostics. Preserve unrelated logic; behaviorally equivalent implementations are valid. Abstract for useful reuse.- Review affected data flow and native calls/configuration. Choose applicable numeric, timing, stale-data, conflict, recovery or loop-response cases. Expected outputs must not be copied from code. Read baselines; failed preconditions invalidate dependent checks. State fixtures; distinguish readback/compile from measured behavior.- PLC logic is NOT a substitute for a certified safety function (IEC 61508 / IEC 62061). Use suitable safety hardware/control. tia_openness_plant_viewWork with the CPM / plant view of a WinCC Unified project (official manual 5.13.2.5 plant view, 5.13.2.6 CPM object instances, 5.13.2.7 interface tags). The plant view belongs to the PROJECT, not to an HMI device: create/delete/rename it, assign the HMI device it belongs to, and build its node tree. Two Create shapes matter and this command picks between them for you: a plain node is PlantViewNodes.Create(name), while a CPM object INSTANCE is PlantViewNodes.Create(name, plant-object-type) - only an instance carries a PlantObject and therefore interface tags. Actions: list (read-only; walks the whole tree recursively and prints each node's path, view path, kind and, for instances, its interface tags with PlcTag/Connection/PlcName/AccessMode/AcquisitionMode/MaxLength), create, delete, rename, assign-device, create-node, delete-node, rename-node, set-interface-tag (manual 5.13.2.7: update an interface tag's name, comment, PLC tag, connection, acquisition mode or access mode on a CPM object INSTANCE, then read the tags back). Rules taken from the manual instead of being discovered the hard way: a project can hold ONLY ONE plant view (create refuses a second one with TIA_PLANT_VIEW_SINGLE_ONLY); assign-device takes the HMI DEVICE ITEM name (the deviceItemName/hmiName that tia_openness_list_hmi_targets reports, e.g. HMI_RT_1) and NOT the station name - a station name is refused by TIA and answered with TIA_PLANT_VIEW_DEVICE_NOT_FOUND plus the real candidates (measured on V20 2026-09-16) - while an EMPTY string clears the assignment and null/whitespace is rejected here because TIA would read it as a device name and answer "device not found"; and interface tags' PlcTag/Connection can only be configured AFTER a device is assigned. Every action except list requires confirm=true. Node paths are "Parent/Child" inside the plant view; an empty node-path addresses the view root, which is where the first node is created. Read back with action=list - the receipt of a mutation is not proof of the tree. THE ACCESS ROUTE IS VERSION-DEPENDENT and the tool resolves both by itself: V20 and earlier expose the composition as a property of the project object (Projects[0].PlantViews, the manual's own sample), while V21 moved the Unified types into their own assembly and with them the CPM surface - reflecting Portal V21's PublicAPI shows PlantViews declared on Siemens.Engineering.HmiUnified.Cpm.PlantViewsProvider and Project implementing Siemens.Engineering.IEngineeringServiceProvider, so the V21 route is Project.GetService<PlantViewsProvider>().PlantViews. The receipt reports which route answered as plantViewRoute, and a version that reaches it neither way answers with every probed route instead of a bare 'not found' (measured live on V21 2026-09-16: create, create-node, list and delete all work through the service route). hierarchyPath reads EMPTY on V21 while viewPath is correct; that is a version behaviour, not a missing node.

tia_hmi_generate_screen_xmlGenerate a Classic HMI SCREEN as SimaticML XML from a structured plan (TIA V16-V21). The XML object shapes come from real exports; this tool does NOT select, attach, or create a TIA screen-template. If the task requires a project screen template, export that target project's real screen-template and use the separate screen-template import round trip. Acceptance still requires import and readback on the selected panel/version. Classic screen authoring uses whole-screen XML: generate, import with tia_openness_import_hmi_xml(kind=screen, device_name), then re-export/read back. Create referenced HMI tags/tables with tia_openness_create_hmi_tag and tia_openness_create_hmi_tag_table (Classic uses XML-backed creation), or import real tag-table XML. Inspect applied/skipped and verify PLC bindings. Screen XML does not set the device start screen: on a confirmed Classic device ask once for Runtime settings > General > Start screen, or reuse a verified configured panel/template. The current bridge cannot write that Classic setting; do not retry guessed attributes. Item fields and examples are in the schema. Alarm/trend/recipe views, illuminated_button and faceplate_instance are refused by this generator; use a separately verified workflow. Set plan.panel_family to check control compatibility: polyline, polygon, slider, gauge, clock and symbol_library require Comfort/Mobile/RT Advanced per the vendor table, even when Basic engineering import accepts them. Gauge/clock use native sizes; supplied width/height are ignored with a warning. Groups require at least two nested items and have no Left/Top. Function keys use plan.function_keys (F1..F8). A Classic button with navigate_to_screen emits the measured Release -> ActivateScreen system-function event; without it the button is label-only. The target screen must already exist or be imported as a companion screen on the same HMI, then the event must be re-exported and clicked in Runtime. Use the actual panel resolution and a free explicit screen number; a duplicate number can terminate TIA and lose unsaved edits. Rendered bounds use the same default sizes as XML generation and are rejected when they leave the canvas. Ordinary overlaps are rejected; nearby row/column controls are warned using plan.min_spacing (default 4). Static Chinese/long labels receive a conservative horizontal-fit warning, but final glyph metrics, layering, navigation and interaction still require a target-resolution Runtime screenshot. Set allow_overlap=true only for an intentional background/decoration layer and review the returned layout summary. If width/height are omitted, 800x480 is only a compatibility default, not the target panel resolution. Unknown fields produce warnings. Generation/import/compile do not prove visual layout or Runtime behavior.

tia_openness_generate_graph_blockGenerate a real GRAPH (sequential function chart) FB as TIA Openness SimaticML XML from a plan of named steps. V16-V21 (machine-verified per-version stamp table): by default each step gets one following transition (Trans{k} unless overridden) and the linear Connections graph S_k -> T_k -> S_{k+1} -> ... -> EndConnection. A step's next jumps its following transition to ANY defined step (self-loop / loop-back / forward jump; a fully-looped block has no EndConnection), and a step's alternatives declares an alternative branch (>=2 competing transitions, each {transition?, condition?, next}) — the Direct/Jump LinkType is derived automatically from the import-verified rule. A step may give a condition (the following transition's condition), an interlock, and/or a supervision — each a series (AND) chain of normally-open contacts; omitted/[] leaves an empty skeleton. A step may also give actions (each a qualifier-tagged target := value assignment), and the plan may declare variables[] (block Static members) so those actions have writable targets and the block compiles clean. The fixed envelope (block AttributeList, GRAPH_BASE interface + standard GRAPH I/O parameters, PreOperations/PostOperations, AlarmsSettings, version stamps) is the import-verified golden verbatim. Writes the .xml when output_path is given (mutating); omit it to get the XML back in the result. Versions other than V16-V21 are rejected with a structured ok:false. The TIA compiler auto-generates the GRAPH runtime block on import; do not hand-write it. Condition/interlock/supervision contacts default to scope GlobalVariable: each such PLC tag must pre-exist as Bool with a bit address (create via tia_openness_create_tags first, or switch to variables[] + scope LocalVariable); the result's requiredGlobalTags field lists them. Local ok:true is shape correctness, not a TIA compile — confirm via tia_openness_import_block_xml + tia_openness_compile. Minimal plan with an action + a loop-back: {"block_name":"FB_Seq","variables":[{"name":"MyOut","datatype":"Bool"}],"steps":[{"name":"Idle","init":true,"actions":[{"qualifier":"N","target":"MyOut","value":"TRUE"}]},{"name":"Run","condition":[{"operand":"INIT_SQ","scope":"LocalVariable"}]},{"name":"Done","next":"Idle"}]}. Alternative-branch plan (2 competing transitions after Idle; each path loops back, so no EndConnection): {"block_name":"FB_Branch","variables":[{"name":"StartA","datatype":"Bool"},{"name":"StartB","datatype":"Bool"}],"steps":[{"name":"Idle","init":true,"alternatives":[{"condition":[{"operand":"StartA","scope":"LocalVariable"}],"next":"PathA"},{"condition":[{"operand":"StartB","scope":"LocalVariable"}],"next":"PathB"}]},{"name":"PathA","next":"Idle"},{"name":"PathB","next":"Idle"}]}.crates\tools\src\builtin_specs\tia_watch_patterns.rs

FIRST call when a simulation step is actually next (project and CPU exist, download is imminent): returns this machine's real simulation capability plus the complete ordered call sequence to reach the goal FOR THE ONE CPU you name. It is the SIMULATION PHASE entry point, not a task-starting survey: do NOT call it before the project and CPU exist, nor front-load it ahead of project creation, hardware, tags, and program generation. One call replaces the probe-and-get-refused loop — it decides the simulator backend, states what that backend can read/write, pre-fills every already-known argument, names the success criterion of EVERY step plus the timing and the recovery (onFailure) of the steps where those apply, and lists environment blockers with the exact user action for each (blockers always carry id/severity/what/evidence/action). MEASURED shape of the emitted steps (recorded R135 plans; 12 steps across 3 plans): successCriterion 12/12 and never empty, onFailure 8/12, timing 5/12 — always present on the executable `go` steps except the read-only route probe and the teardown, so read them rather than assuming every step carries all three. SCOPE (E2E R135): the sequence covers exactly one CPU, because this tool reads no project file and cannot enumerate a project's CPUs — a six-CPU plant project got verdict=go with unknowns=[] and a sequence bound to one CPU, and only that CPU was ever downloaded or simulated. For a multi-CPU project, call tia_openness_list_devices and run this planning step once per CPU; the returned `scope` object says the same thing, and `doNot` forbids reporting a plant-level verdict from one plan. Offline and cheap: it reads the Windows registry and files only, and never starts TIA Portal, PLCSIM or a bridge. Two situations must be told apart before calling: if the project does not exist yet, or exists without its CPU (hardware never created or not read back), do NOT call this tool — create the project and place/read the CPU first, then return here when a simulation step is actually next. If the project already has its CPU and only the route metadata (tia_version, family, project_type_identifier, device_name) is not yet in hand, calling with those fields omitted is allowed: the tool answers with the machine picture plus the exact calls producing the missing facts, then re-plan. | Openness rejects a freshly rebuilt bridge, or a trust dialog reappears | The Openness whitelist is keyed by **file hash**, so a rebuild invalidates it. `FileHash` is base64 SHA256 (not hex) and entries **accumulate**, so "an entry exists" does not mean the current hash is registered. Re-registering needs an administrator and writes under `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE`; there is **no per-user whitelist** (verified: no `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Siemens\Automation\Openness` exists, and `Users` hold read-only rights on the HKLM subtree). But an unregistered client is **questioned, not refused**: Siemens' Openness manual ("TIA Portal Openness firewall") documents that TIA prompts the user, "Yes" allows that ONE connection with no registry write and no elevation, "Yes to all" raises the UAC dialog and writes the entry, and **three refusals raise `EngineeringSecurityException`**. Entries are also keyed by **absolute path**, so a copy of the bridge registered at another path (an older repo checkout, a previous install directory) does not trust the running one. Expect this state after **every** PLC Code update, because publishing rebuilds the bridge. | Confirm with the read-only `tia_openness_check_whitelist` (no administrator needed): the verdict is `hashMatchCount > 0`, never "an entry exists". tia_openness_configure_hmi_mapping_tableConfigure the mapping table of an EXISTING WinCC Unified dynamization (official manual 5.13.2.3 'Accessing simple dynamic'). The vendor's own access path, verbatim: the screen item's Dynamizations are matched on PropertyName, the match is a TagDynamization, and the table hangs off TagDynamization.ValueConverter.MappingTable - so this tool needs a screen item whose property is ALREADY dynamized (bind the tag with tia_openness_create_hmi_screen_item first; this tool will not invent a second way to create a dynamization). Three modes, the three the manual names: range (needs from and to; a single value is from == to), single-bit (needs bit_number; writes the bit's two state rows, condition = state * 2^bit and relevant = 2^bit, with on_value_bool for the set state) and multi-bit (needs bit_number, optional condition/relevant where condition = state * 2^bit and relevant is the decimal mask of the bits used). A row's value is typed by the property itself: give value_color as a decimal "r, g, b" triple for a colour property (e.g. BackColor) or value_bool for a boolean one (e.g. Visible); flashing/flashing_rate/alternate_color map to the row's Flashing/FlashingRate/AlternateValue. One call writes ONE row (single-bit writes that bit's two rows), and the receipt then READS THE TABLE BACK so you see the rows that exist rather than the rows that were intended - every row carries its index, and action=delete-row (with row_index, a from+to pair, or all=true) removes rows again through the vendor's MappingTableEntryBase.Delete(), so a wrong row does not force the whole screen item to be deleted. A row's value type is decided by the slot itself: TIA pre-populates a colour property's row (read back as Color [A=255, ...]), and that current value is what the writer converts to - measured on V21, handing TIA the raw string "0, 200, 0" answers set_Value ... Invalid value type. Range VALUES are validated against the dynamized TAG's data type, not the screen box: measured on V21, a 1..5 range on a BOOL tag compiles with 'Invalid range - the from or to value exceeds the limit for this data type', while 10..20 on an INT tag compiles clean, and overlapping ranges are accepted with the warning 'The range entries of the ... property overlap.' - so pick ranges that fit the tag, then compile to confirm. Unified only: a classic item dynamizes through RangeAppearanceAnimation, a different API, and is refused by name. Requires confirm=true - TIA rejects a wrong row with a property error rather than a crash, and tia_openness_validate_hmi_objects is how you check the result afterwards.

===== RVA 0344BB60 len=2295 =====
siemens_web_api_probeCheck whether one S7-1500/S7-1200 G2 CPU answers on its OFFICIAL Web API (JSON-RPC 2.0, POST https://<host>/api/jsonrpc) and report what that CPU exposes, WITHOUT credentials. This is the second real-machine channel beside siemens_s7_* and it does NOT need PUT/GET communication or non-optimized DBs - the Web API browses and reads symbolically, so it still works on a hardened CPU where siemens_s7_read_values cannot connect at all. Calls only methods that need no authorization: Api.Version (Web API version), Api.Browse (the list of methods THIS CPU firmware actually supports - prefer identity.supportedMethods over guessing from a firmware table), Api.Ping (CPU id), Api.GetAuthenticationMode, Plc.ReadCpuType, Plc.ReadStationName, Plc.ReadModuleName, Plc.ReadSystemTime. No single method is a reachability gate: the endpoint counts as proven once ANY of them answers, and each refusal is reported in unavailableMethods with its documented minimum firmware instead of failing the probe. That matters on S7-1500 R/H redundant CPUs, where Api.Ping and the whole PlcProgram family are documented as not available at all while Api.Version answers normally. Optionally pass user (+password) to also verify the login handshake and return that account's real authorization list from Api.GetPermissions - do this before browse/read/diagnostics to prove the account has read_value / read_diagnostics. CPUs ship a self-signed certificate, so a first call commonly fails with WEBAPI_TLS_UNTRUSTED; re-send with accept_self_signed_certificate=true once you know the target is the intended CPU. Firmware floor (S7-1500 Web server function manual 11/2023, A5E03484625-AK): the Web API exists from V2.8 on S7-1500 standard/T/F CPUs and from V3.1 on S7-1500 R/H; it is not documented for classic S7-1200 V4.x. The S7-1200 G2 has a Web API too, but its versions come from its own manual and are not asserted here. Session tokens are dropped by the CPU after 120 s with no Web API call in the session. The CPU-side prerequisite (Web server enabled + API access allowed) can be set from this software with tia_openness_read_webserver_settings + tia_openness_configure_webserver, then compile and download. Read-only: never writes tags, changes operating mode, or alters CPU configuration.

codesys_sim_assertRun ordered steps against the RUNNING simulated application and report each measured expectation. Simulation proves program logic only, not hardware, fieldbus, wiring or whole-project acceptance. Each step supports write, settleMs or settleScans+scanTimeMs, expect, expectWithinMs, expectNotBeforeMs, holdMs and pollIntervalMs. Each pass requests unique expressions together through native read_values and reuses each result for repeated comparisons; both scalar and batch monitoring can return cached values. observationWindow bounds the HOST API call only; sampleAgeMs is unknown, so it is neither a PLC timestamp nor proof of first-scan/deadline behavior. For short-lived states use a PLC-cycle trace or a test recorder on a copy, preserving control code and driving inputs only; do not infer freshness from a fast API return. A matching read completed after expectWithinMs is undersampled/fail, not timing proof. For short-lived or freshness-limited data, check one expression per fresh stimulus; never extend the program timeout to accommodate slow observation. Use a fixed wait for combinational logic; use expectWithinMs for asynchronous completion, expectNotBeforeMs for a minimum delay, and holdMs to test continued validity. Keep the stimulus write and its measured edge in the same step; sample cadence limits timing resolution. stopOnFirstFailure defaults true; an exhausted sample budget is undersampled, never pass. Forced expressions are refused unless clearForced=true. Preset updates the current session, optionally by verified stop/write/start; neither stop/start nor a fresh login resets scan-carried state, so preset is NEVER proof of power-up defaults. Inspect presetApplied.mechanism, stop/start verification and actual runtime values. Results retain step identity, status, elapsed time, cadence and qualified expressions with expected/actual values. Compact receipts keep complete check lines; oversized reports expose evidence.path and sha256 for the full UTF-8 JSON. If completeResultInline=false, use read_file on that artifact for per-check evidence instead of repeating the simulation. A passing counterexample proves the tested defect, not a good engineering result. Mutating; confirm=run_scenario and disposable=true.

===== RVA 036A2C6C len=2157 =====
Machine-verified (2026-08-16, T07 输送带顺序, V18 + S7-1200 1214C V4.0): three V18 lessons. (1) `.scl` external sources must be pure ASCII — UTF-8 Chinese comments make TIA abort generation with 设定值BEGIN无效 at the line after the comment block; keep block/network comments ASCII. On V19 the same shape is worse when the file has no BOM: TIA silently DROPS the whole FB VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT/VAR interface and every local tag compiles as 'not defined' (the Main OB with VAR_TEMP only still compiled — OB and FB interface parsing differ), so ASCII comments AND a BOM are the safe shape. Also never reference Chinese-named PLC tags from inside an external source (a %I0.0-style absolute address is safe; a 启动-style symbol name mojibakes into 鍚姩 and fails not defined) — Chinese tag NAMES in the tag table itself are fine (T11 2026-08-16: 24 errors from Chinese comments in a VAR block, fixed by ASCII + absolute addresses). (2) On the V18 official-frontend VPLC route, input can only be WRITTEN (whole byte IB0), never read; assert on output QB0 only. (3) The V18 frontend DOES free-run and time advances: 44 assert steps including ~2s and ~4s sequence timing all read back PASS with expect_within_ms windows. A T05 probe once concluded "V18 does not free-run" after polling 4 s and seeing no change — that was a probe defect, not a route limit: keep the stimulus HELD (frontend input writes are not persistent forces), poll with expect_within_ms, and trust the window; do not conclude a timing route is dead from one short poll. V19 behaves like V18. V20 s7-1200 is DIFFERENT: the TON time base does NOT advance with the wall clock (T15 2026-08-16: 8/20/25 s windows never triggered a TON while combinational/latch transitions all verified, even after cold restart) — on V20 assert only the transitions your writes directly cause and confirm timer PT values statically; do not wait for timer outputs, and do not call the program broken over a timer that never fires. (4) Do not build stop-delay logic with TOF: its Q persists ~4 s after the input is forced low and re-energizes outputs after an e-stop reset; use a free-running TON + Time tRef baseline state machine.

tia_openness_create_technology_objectTHE correct way to add a PID_Compact / PID_3Step / PID_Temp control loop or a motion axis (TO_SpeedAxis / TO_PositioningAxis / TO_SynchronousAxis / Cam …) to the active TIA project: it creates a real TECHNOLOGY OBJECT that appears under the device's Technology objects tree and can use the PID/axis commissioning panel. Routes by actual target family: Classic Basic/Comfort uses Siemens native ConnectionComposition.Import and Export verification; Unified uses the existing CLR connection route. New Classic S7-1200/1500 Ethernet connections select the driver using both the actual PLC family and the exact installed HMI hardware catalog entry; Basic and Comfort require different native drivers. Catalog unavailable/unknown panel requires an existing connection or matching native XML. Resolve actual PLC/HMI IP interfaces. OMS Ethernet has no configurable rack/slot parameters: plc_rack/plc_slot are rejected, not silently ignored; actual CPU/rack positions are identity metadata only. Use a distinct connection_name per HMI in the project. Existing connections are reused when no edits are requested; integrated connections cannot be overwritten by XML. Unified: set the address through initial_address — either the complete version-specific string, or a partial "HostAddress=<ip>;PlcAddress=<ip>" which the bridge completes against the connection's existing address. Engineering readback is not live communication or all-version certification.

===== RVA 036F6705 len=1840 =====
On a classic S7-400 CPU, declaring an SCL TON instance and then referencing that instance directly in a boolean expression (e.g. combined with `AND`, or passed where a Bool is expected) fails to compile. The compiler treats the instance as its own type (`Block_SFB`), not as the timer's `Q` output, and three different call/declaration syntaxes for the same intent all hit the identical two-part error. Separately, an equivalent TON_TIME network built as LAD/SimaticML XML imports and compiles with 0 errors — but that only proves syntactic validity, not runtime timing: on the real classic PLCSIM target the OB1 scan cycle is fast enough that a T#200ms timer had still not triggered after 2330 scan cycles. The workaround that worked first try in that session: drop the timer instruction entirely and implement the delay as a DINT scan-cycle counter incremented by 1 every OB1 pass, compared against a threshold computed as (desired delay time / an estimated per-cycle time); this is plain SCL (about 40 lines) with no SFB/timer instance involved. Note what that session did NOT establish: it is not evidence that a classic CPU refuses IEC timers — the same CPU compiled the LAD `TON_TIME` network with 0 errors, and the type error is the documented member-access shape (`tia_openness_write_source`'s real-import-verified grammar for V16-V21: declare `TON_TIME`/`TP_TIME`/`TOF_TIME`/`TONR_TIME`, call `#Inst.TON(IN := …, PT := …)` with `PT` mandatory, then read `#Inst.Q`/`#Inst.ET`; an OB interface is `VAR_TEMP`/`VAR CONSTANT` only, so the instance has to live in an FB or a global instance DB). Also note the counter's own cost: a scan-cycle delay drifts with scan load, so its threshold has to be recomputed against a measured cycle time and verified on the target — the same discipline the 2330-cycle observation demands of the timer.

mitsubishi_mc_read_bitsRead consecutive BIT devices from a Mitsubishi PLC over the MC protocol (MELSEC Communication) 3E frame - batch read (command 0401, bit units). Reads count consecutive points starting at address. Supported bit devices: X, Y, M, L, F, V, B, S, SB, SM, DX, DY, plus the timer/counter contacts and coils TS, TC, CS, CC, STS, STC (a Mitsubishi timer is three separate devices - contact TS, coil TC, current value TN - so the bare name T addresses none of them and is refused with that explanation; same for C and ST). Device numbers follow the MELSEC-Q/L/iQ-R convention: X, Y, B, SB, DX, DY are HEXADECIMAL (X1A, B1234), while M, L, F, V, S, SM and the timer/counter devices are DECIMAL (M100). Every result reports the radix it used in addressRadix; on FX5/iQ-F the X/Y radix is instead a per-connection message-format setting (X,Y OCT vs X,Y HEX), which the result flags in addressRadixWarning. count is 1..3584 (the MC protocol hard limit for a single bit-unit batch read); read more by issuing several calls. A word device (D/W/R/TN/etc.) is refused with a pointer to mitsubishi_mc_read_words. UNVERIFIED: this MC channel has NOT been tested on a real Mitsubishi PLC and cannot be on the current bench (no Mitsubishi PLC, no GX Works installed) - the frame codec is proven offline only against the byte-level communication examples and the device-code table in the official MELSEC Communication Protocol Reference Manual SH(NA)-080008-AB, and every result says verified:false. The CPU answers MC only after the MC/SLMP connection is opened in GX Works Ethernet parameters and downloaded; connection errors explain this. transport is tcp (default) or udp. 3E frame only. READ ONLY - there is no write path in this channel.

启动画面（Classic 的硬边界，先读完这段再动手）：Classic 根本没有可写的启动画面 API。V18 实机逐对象实测：HmiTarget 只有 Author/Name 两个属性，StartScreen/StartupScreen/RuntimeSettings 全部回答 "not supported by type"，`<device>/HMI/RuntimeSettings` 路径本身不存在；本机 V15.1–V21 六套 Openness 公开 API 文档里 StartScreen 只出现在 Unified 一侧，V21 的 classic 程序集 Siemens.Engineering.WinCC.dll 里连这个字符串都没有。因此调用 set_hmi_start_screen 在 Classic 上一定返回 TIA_HMI_CLASSIC_START_SCREEN_API_UNAVAILABLE —— 换属性名、换工具、反复导入画面 XML 都不会改变（画面 XML 不携带该值），CAx 也带不走（TIA 导出时直接跳过 HMI 设备，AML 只有空壳）。不要在这上面反复试探调用或让用户等你去研究。两条可行路径：①请用户点一次——TIA 里选中该 HMI 设备 → 运行系统设置 → 常规 → 起始画面 → 选画面并保存（每台设备一次，属于设备级运行设置）；②复用一个已经配置好的面板——create_from_master_copy 从工程库/全局库母版实例化会保留启动画面（V18 实测：实例出来的两台面板编译均 0 错 0 警告），整工程存档/起始工程同样带走。在那之前 Classic 编译恰好只有 1 个错误：`Runtime settings: No start screen defined or the start screen has been deleted.`；不得把这一编译错误描述成"画面已经全部合格"，也不得声称软件已能自动设置。

从完整走通的 S7-400 LAD 项目（锂电池叠片机，73 网络状态机）与三后端实测沉淀。classic S7-300/400 仿真恒走 S7-PLCSIM V5.4（S7ProSim COM），任何博图版本 V16-V21 相同，且没有 WCF/vplc/Advanced 替代路线（那些仿真器不能仿真 300/400）。该后端的硬限制：SingleScan 下 IEC 定时器不推进、执行节流（请求扫描数不等于实际完成数）、两次工具调用之间 CPU 执行 0 周期（sidecar 断开回退 SingleScan）。三条硬规则：(1) 定时等待用扫描计数代替 TON——static Int 每扫描 +1，非激活时清零，Ge(计数, 阈值) 判完成；阈值=等效扫描数（仿真用小值如 1/1/30，真实机器按扫描周期换算如 10ms/scan 时 0.5s≈50 scans）。(2) 内部诊断（步骤解码/忙/完成位）一律映射到未用的 Q 区输出位——Q 区是所有后端通用的唯一可靠读回通道（classic 的 M 区读回不可靠；V16-WCF/V18-官方后端连 I/M/DB 都读不了）。刺激写入必须显式传 scan_cycles，实际执行数用 Q 区计数读回推断，绝不信请求数。验证三问——程序"没动"时按顺序：(1) 执行确认：无条件递增计数读两次是否增长？不增长=CPU 没跑（下载失败/STOP/会话断），不是逻辑问题；(2) 状态确认：当前步骤解码字是什么？先知道状态再怀疑逻辑；(3) 逻辑确认：①②正常才查网络。已知坑：步骤转换在扫描末尾执行→输出滞后一拍（多扫一次再读）；每次下载清空 DB/M（别把初始状态当运行结果）；硬件 NC 停止/急停（1=正常）在 LAD 必须用 NO 触点；TONR 经典目标不可用（用 TON + 步骤差分复位门控）。
